label: First step on a token from a fixed set, plus the first copy step (re-reading token 0) when L=3
explanation: Fires in two position-locked contexts. (1) At t=0 whenever the first token is one of d,e,h,i,k,m,n,p,q,t,u,v,x,1,2. This set is deterministic: precision is 1.0 for each of these tokens and 0 for the other 15. Activation here is small and depends on the token (k,u,v,q highest, about 0.15-0.17 of max; t,p,2 lowest). This is about 80% of active steps but only 68% of activation mass. (2) At the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx=1, input = token 0, output = token 1) in short sequences. It is strongest at L=3, where it fires for any token and produces the largest activations (top examples near the max of 0.27). It fires more weakly and only sometimes at L=4. It never fires at the delimiter step, at original positions t>=2, or at copy steps with recall_idx>=3. Weak residual firing at t=1 and recall_idx=2 makes up the misses.

issues: The factual claims hold. At t=0 the unit covers 80% of active steps and 68% of activation mass. It is silent on the delimiter step and on original positions t>=2. The recall_idx>=3 steps are essentially silent (13 active steps on dev). On test the predicate has 0 false positives (precision 1.0, F1 0.916).

A systematic class of misses remains. At recall_idx==1 with L==4 there are about 5.8k active steps on dev, carrying about 8.4% of activation mass. These are not random: when the re-read token 0 is in the same 15-token set as the t=0 context, precision is 0.59 and they hold 7% of mass. When it is outside that set, precision is 0.21. The explanation calls L=4 firing weak and only occasional and leaves it out, but it does not mention that the L=4 firing follows the same token set.

The label only mentions L=3. It leaves out that the first-copy-step context spreads to L=4, gated by token identity. There is also a smaller miss class at recall_idx==2 with L==3 (about 3.6% of mass).
Adding (recall_idx==1)&(L==4)&isin(in_tok,SET) raises test F1 from 0.916 to 0.932 and mass recall from 0.88 to 0.95, with precision 0.95.
